issues.description: Per-file fact index, one daemon per machine with a priority queue, MCP over stateless Streamable HTTP, CLI — in **Kotlin/JVM** (user decision 2026-10-07; CL-56). Base index of the default branch built from git objects in a short-lived child JVM. The Node.js prototype (CL-9) measured: Terrio 2,211 files in 5.4 s, worker peak 567 MB, DB 57 MB, daemon 80 MB, query 9–31 ms — the Kotlin port must match or beat it within the JVM budgets in CL-56. Analysis: docs/analysis.md, plan: docs/plan.md (repo Terrio-cz/CodeLoupe; KB articles in this project).

Index the tracker like code: issues, epics, links and dependencies, fields, acceptance criteria, comments, and the code each task touched — kept fresh by a cheap watcher, queried by agents in one compact call. Serves reading (brief/sections/delta), the dispatcher (ready tasks, collisions with active worktrees), the planner (one context pack) and issue creation (duplicate check). Measured 2026-09-23 → 10-06: YouTrack tool results = 1.97 % of all agent cost; the dispatcher (terrio-suggester) spends 20 % of its cost on YouTrack (1,441 calls in 117 runs, ~12 per run) and predicts code collisions by hand with GitNexus/rg; issues are read 6.5× on average; yt_search 944 calls, yt_create_issue 204. Generic: a tracker adapter interface with YouTrack first (GitHub Issues/Jira possible later); Terrio workflow rules stay in the Terrio layer. Analysis: docs/analysis.md § 5.

issues.summary: Worktree overlays and lazy base sync
issues.description:
## Context
Answers must reflect the worktree being worked on, not only the default branch.

## Scope
Overlay DB per worktree = files differing from base commit B (git diff --name-status B + untracked, tombstones); check on query (git status + mtime/size), no watchers; lazy base sync when the default branch moves (inline ≤ 200 files, else heavy lane); GC of overlays whose worktree is gone.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Changed/new/deleted file visible in the next query
- [x] Default branch moved by 500 files → correct answers, sync in the heavy lane
- [x] Zero CPU when idle
- [x] Overlay removed when its worktree disappears

## Verification
Integration tests with a temp repo and two worktrees.

issues.summary: Local YouTrack mirror with incremental watcher
issues.description:
## Context
Issues are re-read 6.5× on average.

## Scope
SQLite mirror behind a tracker adapter interface (YouTrack first): issues, epics, fields, links, parsed acceptance criteria, comments, attachment metadata, history of state changes; full-text index (SQLite FTS5) over summary, description and comments; watcher polls `updated` per configured project every 2–5 min only while clients are active; freshness check by `updated` on read.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Mirror stays within 5 min of YouTrack while windows run
- [ ] No polling when idle
- [ ] Credentials never logged or returned

## Verification
Integration test against a test project; status shows last sync.

issues.summary: Port CodeLoupe to Kotlin/JVM with parity to phase 1
issues.description:
## Context
The user chose Kotlin (2026-10-07): it is the language they know and want to read. Phase 1 exists as a Node.js prototype (commit b7d0166, CL-9): it is the behavioural reference and is removed once the Kotlin version reaches parity. Performance expectation: queries equal (SQLite-bound), base build faster with a native parser, daemon RAM higher than Node (80 MB) — budgets below.

## Scope
1. **Parser spike first** — on all 2,211 Terrio Kotlin files measure parse-all time, peak RSS, files with syntax errors and artifact size for: (a) Kotlin compiler PSI, parse only (org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-compiler-embeddable, stable 2.4.x line); (b) tree-sitter-ng (io.github.bonede:tree-sitter 0.26.x + tree-sitter-kotlin 0.3.8.1, JNI natives bundled); (c) jtreesitter 0.26.1 (FFM, Java 22+, grammar native lib must be built per OS). Record the decision and numbers in docs/plan.md. Java support (CL-11) must stay possible with the chosen route.
2. **Gradle Kotlin DSL project** in the same repo, Maven Central only, non-interactive Gradle, toolchain JDK 25 (JetBrains Runtime 25 is in ~/.gradle/jdks; system JAVA_HOME is JDK 17 — never rely on it). One top-level type per file, package = folder, small single-purpose classes (the user's Kotlin rules).
3. **Port**: extractor (decls, imports, refs with kinds/receivers/enclosing decl), SQLite store via org.xerial:sqlite-jdbc (same schema), base build from git objects in a child JVM (-Xmx512m, low priority, one at a time), registry (git common dir → repo, default branch, .codeloupe.json), priority queue with coalescing (coroutines), View with overlay masking, find/outline/symbol with identical output format, daemon (Ktor, 127.0.0.1, Host/Origin/x-codeloupe checks, Connection: close, /status, /api/<tool>, /shutdown, calls.jsonl), MCP over stateless Streamable HTTP via io.modelcontextprotocol:kotlin-sdk-server 0.15.x (or a minimal own JSON-RPC handler if the SDK cannot do stateless), CLI (clikt) with daemon autostart and mcp-config.
4. **Tests**: port the 17 Node tests to kotlin.test/JUnit 5 with the same fixtures; repeat the headless Claude Code restart check.
5. **Remove the Node prototype** (src/, bin/, package.json, node tests) in the last commit; README and docs updated.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Parser decision recorded with measured numbers for all three options
- [x] Kotlin output of find/outline/symbol identical to the Node prototype on the fixtures and on 10 Terrio queries
- [x] Terrio base build ≤ 10 s, build worker peak ≤ 600 MB
- [x] Daemon steady RSS ≤ 200 MB (JVM flags tuned: SerialGC, small heap, CDS), query p95 ≤ 50 ms warm
- [x] MCP works from Claude Code and survives a daemon restart (headless check)
- [x] All ported tests green; Node prototype removed

## Verification
gradlew test; Terrio measurements attached; headless claude -p restart check attached.

issues.summary: Task graph queries: tasks, task_graph, ready, epic_progress
issues.description:
## Context
Measured 2026-09-23 → 10-06: YouTrack tool results = 1.97 % of all agent cost; the dispatcher (terrio-suggester) spends 20 % of its cost on YouTrack (1,441 calls in 117 runs, ~12 per run) and predicts code collisions by hand with GitNexus/rg; issues are read 6.5× on average; yt_search 944 calls, yt_create_issue 204.

## Scope
`tasks(query)` — YouTrack-like filters + full-text, one line per task (id, state, type, priority, epic, title, blockers); `task_graph(id, depth)` — epic, subtasks, depends-on / required-for, relates, duplicates with states; `ready(scope)` — open tasks whose dependencies are resolved and that no active workspace holds (CL-66); `epic_progress(epic)` — counts by state, open criteria, blockers. All from the local index, compact text.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each query answers from the index in < 100 ms
- [ ] ready() matches a manual check on 3 Terrio epics
- [ ] Output ≤ 1 line per task

## Verification
Tests on a fixture tracker dump + Terrio TER.

issues.summary: Task ↔ code links from git history and descriptions
issues.description:
## Context
Which tasks touched this code, and which code will this task touch, are answered today by reading commits and grepping.

## Scope
Landed tasks: commits/merges with `TER-<n>` (configurable pattern) → changed files and declarations via the code index (changes() of CL-17). Open tasks: predicted touch set from paths, modules, symbols and API routes mentioned in the description and acceptance criteria, resolved against the code index (confidence labels). Queries: `task_code(id)`, `code_tasks(symbol|path)`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Landed TER tasks map to their declarations
- [ ] Predicted touch sets carry confidence and evidence
- [ ] code_tasks lists prior tasks for a symbol with merge SHAs

## Verification
Spot check on 10 landed and 10 open TER tasks.

issues.summary: Dispatcher support: collision prediction and window grouping
issues.description:
## Context
The dispatcher must never put two windows on the same code; today it predicts this manually.

## Scope
`dispatch_plan(candidates | epic | query, slots)` — ready tasks, predicted touch sets vs. active worktrees and each other, groups colliding tasks into one window (batch ≤ 3 small or a chain), keeps windows clear of live ones; explains every grouping in one line. The Terrio suggester keeps the final judgment and `run/terrio.mjs suggest check`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Plans for 3 recent Terrio dispatches match or beat the manual ones
- [ ] Each grouping cites the shared code
- [ ] Suggester cost per run drops (metrics)

## Verification
Replay 3 recorded dispatcher sessions; codeloupe metrics compare.

## Context
Planners read the issue, linked issues, prior tasks and code in many calls.

## Scope
One call: brief issue with acceptance criteria, linked and dependency issues (brief), prior tasks touching the same code (summary, merge SHA), the relevant declarations (outline lines, not bodies) and open criteria from related tasks; sections selectable; delta mode when called again.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One call replaces the planner's issue/related/search round trips
- [ ] Second call on an unchanged task < 100 tokens

## Verification
Planner benchmark (CL-23) with and without the pack.

issues.summary: Duplicate and related check before creating an issue
issues.description:
## Context

## Scope

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Top 5 similar issues returned in < 100 ms
- [ ] Terrio creation flow (orchestrator, steward) calls it

## Verification
Replay of 20 recent creations: how many had a likely duplicate.
